claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of the UK government guidance, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**Key Issue:** While Alex meets the age requirement (10 years old, under 16), and you live in the UK, Alex does not live with you. In this situation, you need to contribute at least as much as the Child Benefit payment amount toward's Alex's upkeep to be considered "responsible" for them.

**The problem:** 
- Current Child Benefit rate for an only/eldest child: **£25.60 per week**
- Your weekly contribution toward Alex's upkeep: **£20.00 per week**
- Shortfall: **£5.60 per week**

To qualify for Child Benefit when a child doesn't live with you, you must pay at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (or equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - this includes food, clothes, pocket money, and financial contributions for accommodation.

**What you could do:**
If you're able to increase your contribution to at least £25.60 per week (or the equivalent in kind), you would meet the eligibility criteria and could claim Child Benefit for Alex. Otherwise, the person Alex lives with should be the one claiming Child Benefit, as only one person can claim for each child.

reasonings:
According to the UK government guidance, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You'll usually be responsible for a child if either: (1) you live with them, OR (2) you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money.

For Alex:
- Alex is 10 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- Alex does not live with you ✗
- You contribute £20.00 per week towards Alex's upkeep

The critical issue is whether £20.00 per week meets the threshold requirement. According to the guidance on children living with someone else, you can continue to get payments if you 'contribute to your child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment.'

The current Child Benefit rates are:
- £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child
- £16.95 per week for additional children

Since Alex is the only child you're claiming for, you would need to contribute at least £25.60 per week to qualify. Your contribution of £20.00 per week falls short of this requirement by £5.60.

Therefore, you do not meet the financial contribution threshold required to be considered 'responsible' for Alex under the Child Benefit rules.
